feed.description: Long-form conversations about sustainability, systems thinking, and the ideas shaping our shared future.
feed.title: The Long View

bullets: Sustainability is a systems-thinking problem before it's an environmental problem — internalizing this makes downstream decisions easier, while ignoring it means rebuilding the approach from scratch a year later.
The most expensive thing about climate is the optionality lost by delaying rather than the direct cost of acting; the second-order effect of that delay is the part most people miss.
Risk management at planetary scale looks like reliability engineering at company scale — a pattern observed holding across three different teams using Carbon Trust.
Carbon accounting needs the rigor that double-entry bookkeeping brought to finance, rather than looser estimation practices.
Adopting Carbon Trust within a workflow makes trade-offs visible; the framing matters because it reveals which trade-offs are actually being made.
Project Drawdown is one of the platforms where the systems-thinking pattern shows up cleanly, alongside Carbon Trust and IEA as reference points for teams.
Reliability trade-offs cross-cut every other sustainability decision, making reliability a unifying lens rather than a separate concern.
Running one idea for two weeks is the recommended starting point — progress comes from iteration rather than comprehensive upfront adoption.
